text: 怎样避免活在信息茧房之中？
en: How to avoid living in an information cocoon?

text: 郭德纲讲过一个段子。
en: Guo Degang once told a joke.

text: 一群外国人偷了财宝，被军阀抓住。
en: A group of foreigners stole treasures and were caught by a warlord.

text: 语言不通，只能请于谦老爷子当翻译。
en: Unable to communicate, they could only ask Old Master Yu Qian to translate.

text: 老外为了活命，把财宝藏在哪儿，全交代了。
en: To save their lives, the foreigners confessed everything about where the treasures were hidden.

text: 结果老爷子转头对军阀说：“他们宁死不屈，还骂您，让您有种就崩了他们。
en: As a result, the old master turned to the warlord and said: 'They would rather die than yield, and they curse you, daring you to shoot them if you have the guts.

text: ”军阀大怒，当场把人全杀了。
en: ' The warlord flew into a rage and killed them all on the spot.

text: 晚上，老爷子扛着铁锨，把财宝全挖回自己家。
en: At night, the old master, carrying a shovel, dug all the treasures back to his own home.

text: 这个段子最狠的地方，不是黑色幽默。
en: The most ruthless part of this joke is not the black humour.

text: 它揭示了一件事：真正决定结局的，不是谁有暴力，也不是谁有财富，而是谁掌握信息通道。
en: It reveals one thing: what truly decides the outcome is not who has violence, nor who has wealth, but who controls the information channel.

text: 军阀以为自己听到了真话，其实他听到的只是翻译想让他听的版本。
en: The warlord thought he heard the truth, but what he heard was only the version the translator wanted him to hear.

text: 外国人以为自己已经把真相说清楚了，可他们的信息根本没有抵达对方。
en: The foreigners thought they had explained the truth clearly, but their information never reached the other party at all.

text: 两边都以为自己在面对现实，实际上面对的，都是被篡改过的现实。
en: Both sides thought they were facing reality, but what they actually faced was doctored reality.

text: 这就是信息茧房最可怕的地方——你根本意识不到自己接收到的已经被加工过了。
en: This is the most terrifying aspect of information cocoons — you don't even realise what you receive has been processed.

text: 很多人对“信息茧房”的理解太浅了。
en: Many people's understanding of 'information cocoons' is too shallow.

text: 以为只是平台算法推送同质化内容，越看越窄。
en: They think it is just platforms' algorithms pushing homogenised content, making one's view narrower the more one watches.

text: 确实，2023年中国青年报的一项调查显示，62.2%的受访者直言“大数据+算法”的精准推送让自己陷入了信息茧房。
en: Indeed, a 2023 China Youth Daily survey showed that 62.2% of respondents bluntly said that 'big data + algorithm' precise pushing had trapped them in information cocoons.

text: 但这只是表面。
en: But this is only the surface.

text: 更致命的信息茧房，是你以为自己获得了信息，但你得到的只是别人精心处理过的版本。
en: The more deadly information cocoon is when you think you have obtained information, but what you get is only a version carefully processed by others.

text: 你听到的，是别人想让你听见的那部分；你看到的，是别人愿意让你看到的那个角落。
en: What you hear is the part others want you to hear; what you see is the corner others are willing to let you see.

text: 那怎么破？
en: So how do we break it?

text: 信息茧房的本质是共鸣成瘾。
en: The essence of information cocoons is resonance addiction.

text: 从心理舒适度出发，人们会倾向于相信那些能与自己的经历、情绪、身份产生共鸣的信息，无论它是否真的有道理。
en: Starting from psychological comfort, people tend to believe information that resonates with their experiences, emotions and identities, whether or not it really makes sense.

text: 自洽和舒适感所带来的多巴胺，会阻止你用理性去推测表面信息背后的逻辑。
en: The dopamine brought by self-consistency and comfort prevents you from rationally inferring the logic behind surface information.

text: 所以企图靠“多刷点不一样的内容”来破茧，效果有限。
en: So attempting to break cocoons by 'scrolling more different content' has limited effect.

text: 你会发现自己刷了一圈，最后还是回到了让自己舒服的圈子里。
en: You will find that after scrolling around, you still return to the circle that makes you comfortable.

text: 真正能用的方法，其实不需要你每天花几个小时去对抗算法。
en: Methods that truly work don't actually require you to spend hours every day fighting algorithms.

text: 第一层，学会解析信息的底层逻辑。
en: First level: learn to parse the underlying logic of information.

text: 看到一条让你激动或者愤怒的消息，试着把它里的形容词和情绪词全部去掉。
en: When you see a message that excites or angers you, try removing all adjectives and emotional words from it.

text: 比如“无良企业压榨员工”“善良大妈遭报应”，去掉修饰词后，剩下的核心事实是什么？
en: For example, 'unscrupulous companies exploit employees' or 'kind old ladies get retribution' — after removing modifiers, what are the remaining core facts?

text: 很多时候你会发现，一旦剥离了情绪包装，信息的可信度就大打折扣。
en: Often you will find that once the emotional packaging is stripped away, the credibility of the information drops greatly.

text: 这不是让你变得冷漠，而是帮你躲开那些精心设计的情绪钩子。
en: This is not asking you to become indifferent, but helping you dodge those carefully designed emotional hooks.

text: 第二层，用合订本复盘。
en: Second level: review with bound volumes.

text: 那些曾经让你产生巨大共鸣或情绪刺激的信息，在热点消退之后，翻出来重新看一遍。
en: For information that once produced huge resonance or emotional stimulation in you, after the hotspot fades, dig it out and re-read it.

text: 问自己几个问题：我当时为什么信了？
en: Ask yourself a few questions: why did I believe it at the time?

text: 我的共鸣点在哪里？
en: Where was my resonance point?

text: 后来有没有反转？
en: Was there a reversal later?

text: 现在的我回头看，当时漏掉了哪些信息？
en: Looking back now, what information did I miss at the time?

text: 复旦大学新闻学院副教授翁之颢说过，反复接触同质化信息会让思考问题的视角变得单一。
en: Weng Zhihao, associate professor at Fudan University's School of Journalism, said that repeated exposure to homogenised information makes one's perspective on problems singular.

text: 合订本复盘就是在帮你把那个单一的视角打开一个口子。
en: Bound-volume review helps you open a gap in that singular perspective.

text: 第三层，有意识地寻找对立面。
en: Third level: consciously seek the opposite side.

text: 注意，不是让你去跟人对骂，而是分析对立观点的合理之处。
en: Note: this is not asking you to curse at people, but to analyse the rationality of opposing views.

text: 比如你强烈支持某个政策，那就找一篇反对它的高质量文章，认真读，看看对方的论据是什么，逻辑链条是否成立。
en: For example, if you strongly support a policy, find a high-quality article opposing it, read it seriously, and see what the other party's arguments are and whether their logical chain holds.

text: 不是要你改变立场，而是让你知道自己站在哪、脚下的地基有多厚。
en: It is not asking you to change your stance, but to let you know where you stand and how thick the ground under your feet is.

text: 很多人的“信念”其实经不起这样的考验，一推就倒。
en: Many people's 'beliefs' actually cannot withstand such tests — one push and they collapse.

text: 这种推倒不是坏事，它能让你从情绪认同转向理性判断。
en: This kind of collapse is not a bad thing; it allows you to shift from emotional identification to rational judgment.

text: 第四层，极简化和反向代入。
en: Fourth level: extreme simplification and reverse role-play.

text: 把你认可的信息向极端方向推演，看会不会出现明显的谬误。
en: Push information you agree with towards extremes, and see if obvious fallacies appear.

text: 比如“只要努力就能成功”这个观点很正能量，但极端推演就会变成“不成功就是不努力”，这是荒谬的。
en: For example, the view 'hard work leads to success' is very positive, but extreme deduction turns it into 'lack of success means lack of effort', which is absurd.

text: 同样，把你习惯代入的角色换成对立面——如果你是那篇新闻里的“反派”，你会怎么想？
en: Similarly, swap the role you habitually play for the opposite side — if you were the 'villain' in that news article, what would you think?

text: 这种思维训练能帮你跳出条件反射式的站队。
en: This kind of thinking training helps you jump out of reflexive taking-sides.

text: 不过说这些，可能还是有点抽象。
en: But saying all this may still be a bit abstract.

text: 具体到操作层面，其实平台已经给了你不少工具，只是你没用。
en: Specifically at the operational level, platforms have actually given you quite a few tools — you just haven't used them.

text: 中央网信办持续加强信息推荐算法治理，抖音、小红书、微博、快手等平台都上线了“内容偏好评估”和“一键破茧”功能。
en: The Cyberspace Administration of China continues to strengthen governance of information recommendation algorithms, and platforms such as Douyin, Xiaohongshu, Weibo and Kuaishou have all launched 'content preference assessment' and 'one-click cocoon breaking' functions.

text: 你可以去设置里找到“个性化推荐”开关，直接关掉它。
en: You can go into settings, find the 'personalised recommendation' switch, and directly turn it off.

text: 也可以点击“不感兴趣”或“我不喜欢”来告诉算法：我不想再看这类内容。
en: You can also click 'not interested' or 'I don't like it' to tell the algorithm: I don't want to see this kind of content anymore.

text: 上海市委网信办发布的算法治理小贴士里，三个建议非常直接：主动关闭个性化推荐、使用负反馈功能、自主调节兴趣标签。
en: In the algorithm governance tips issued by the Shanghai Municipal Cyberspace Administration, three suggestions are very direct: proactively turn off personalised recommendations, use negative feedback functions, and independently adjust interest tags.

text: 你完全可以在几分钟内切断算法的喂养通道。
en: You can completely cut off the algorithm's feeding channel within a few minutes.

text: 但最核心的问题可能不在技术层面。
en: But the core problem may not be at the technical level.

text: 很多人宁愿待在茧房里，是因为茧房让人舒服，让人觉得自己是对的，让人不用面对世界的复杂。
en: Many people would rather stay in cocoons because cocoons are comfortable, make people feel they are right, and spare them from facing the complexity of the world.

text: 如果你真的想避免信息茧房，就必须接受一个前提：你对世界的理解永远是不完整的，你持有的观点永远有被推翻的可能。
en: If you truly want to avoid information cocoons, you must accept a premise: your understanding of the world is always incomplete, and the views you hold always have the possibility of being overturned.

text: 这种不确定性会让很多人焦虑，但成熟的人到最后都会警惕那个“垄断解释权”的角色——不管是算法、大V，还是你身边的某个权威。
en: This uncertainty makes many people anxious, but mature people will eventually be wary of that role that 'monopolises the right to interpret' — whether algorithms, big Vs, or some authority around you.

text: 能看原文，就别只看转述。
en: If you can read the original text, don't only read retellings.

text: 能见当事人，就别只听中间人。
en: If you can meet the people involved, don't only listen to intermediaries.

text: 能核实事实，就别急着被情绪带走。
en: If you can verify facts, don't rush to be carried away by emotions.

text: 因为很多时候，真正决定你命运的，不是你站在哪一边，而是你到底还有没有能力绕过“翻译”，直接看见现实。
en: Because often, what truly decides your fate is not which side you stand on, but whether you still have the ability to bypass the 'translator' and directly see reality.

text: 最可怕的，从来不是信息太少。
en: The most terrifying thing has never been too little information.

text: 而是有人站在你和真相之间，还让你以为自己看见了全部。
en: It is that someone stands between you and the truth, yet makes you think you have seen everything.

text: 1，所有信息均存疑。
en: 1. Treat all information as doubtful.

text: 不要投入100%信任
en: Don't invest 100% trust.

text: 2，多方验证，尤其是正反两方。
en: 2. Verify from multiple sides, especially both positive and negative sides.

text: 孤证不立。
en: Isolated evidence does not stand.

text: 很多信息，无法多方验证，那就先半信半疑。
en: For much information that cannot be verified from multiple sides, first be half-sceptical.

text: 不要投入100%信任
en: Don't invest 100% trust.

text: 多方验证有门槛，需要你自己有主动性、积极性、知识水平
en: Multi-side verification has thresholds: it requires your own initiative, enthusiasm and knowledge level.

text: 3，要有记性，要看历史合订本。
en: 3. Have a memory; look at historical bound volumes.

text: 不少真相的浮现，需要时间
en: The emergence of many truths takes time.

text: 真相浮现的时候，你要记得，你第一次接触信息的时候，哪个信息源是如何描述信息的
en: When truth emerges, you must remember how each information source described the information when you first encountered it.

text: 4，持续筛选、评级信息源。
en: 4. Continuously filter and rate information sources.

text: 所有媒体、所有信息源都是有立场、有技巧的
en: All media and all information sources have stances and techniques.

text: 在前3步基础上，真相浮现的时候，你要复盘信息所涉及的所有信息源
en: On the basis of the first 3 steps, when truth emerges, you must review all information sources involved in the information.

text: 比较客观的信息源，加分
en: Relatively objective information sources get points added.

text: 说假话、乱说的信息源，减分
en: Information sources that lie or talk nonsense get points deducted.

text: 逐渐积累优质信息源，远离、排除劣质信息源
en: Gradually accumulate high-quality information sources, and stay away from and exclude low-quality information sources.

text: 5，信息包括事实、观点
en: 5. Information includes facts and views.

text: 为了避免信息茧房，要刻意、刻意、刻意保留观点不同、甚至相反的信息源（左右之分、中外之分）
en: To avoid information cocoons, deliberately, deliberately, deliberately retain information sources with different, even opposite views (left-right distinctions, Chinese-foreign distinctions).

text: 注意，观点可以不同，但对同一事实的认定要大致是一致的，不能对着事实说假话
en: Note: views may differ, but the determination of the same fact must be roughly consistent; you cannot lie about facts.

text: 说假事实、故意指鹿为马的信息源，不管观点如何，一律排除
en: Information sources that state false facts or deliberately call a deer a horse, regardless of their views, are all excluded.
